title: Testing model-dependent behaviour
outcome: Explain testing model-dependent behaviour using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Judge two summaries with a rubric. A summariser must preserve two supplied facts and use at most 20 words.
given: Facts: club meets Friday, room B. Recorded replies: "Friday in room B" and "Friday in room D".

steps.label: Identify facts
steps.detail: The answer must retain Friday and room B.

steps.label: Check first reply
steps.detail: Its four words preserve both supplied facts.

steps.label: Check second reply
steps.detail: It is short, but room D contradicts room B.

explanation: A behaviour contract can accept different wording while requiring the same facts. Short, fluent text may still fail factual support.

counterfactual.change: Use a 25-word answer that preserves both facts.
counterfactual.prediction: It passes support but fails the length requirement.
counterfactual.reason: Every mandatory criterion must pass; facts do not erase a length violation.

student_task: Score "Friday in room B" and "Friday in room D" against both mandatory criteria. Would a correct 25-word response pass, and why?
teacher_answer: The answer must retain Friday and room B. Its four words preserve both supplied facts. It is short, but room D contradicts room B. Changed case: It passes support but fails the length requirement. Every mandatory criterion must pass; facts do not erase a length violation.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: Two recorded replies do not estimate future reliability; define run conditions and test wider case coverage.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
